# 2) For each note, parse movie titles whose following/paired line indicates director: Peter Jackson
jackson_titles = []
for nid in note_ids:
    note = apis.simple_note.show_note(note_id=nid, access_token=simple_token)
    content = note.get('content','')
    # parse patterns in the note content
    # We'll look for lines starting with '-' optionally preceded by spaces, then a title line followed by ' - director: ...'
    # Simpler: iterate over lines and detect "director: Peter Jackson" then take most recent title line that doesn't start with ' - director:'
    lines = [ln.rstrip() for ln in content.splitlines()]
    last_title = None
    for ln in lines:
        stripped = ln.strip()
        if stripped.startswith('-') and 'director:' not in stripped:
            # treat bullet line with movie title
            # movie title lines in this note look like "-director"? Actually "The Lord of..." without dash, then next lines are bullets.
            # So handle both: a line that does not contain ':' and not starting with '-'? We'll handle after.
            pass
        # Detect a movie title line: starts with 'The ' etc; in this note they are plain lines, then next indented bullet lines begin with '- director:'
        if stripped and not stripped.startswith('-') and ':' not in stripped and stripped.lower() != 'movie recommendations':
            # candidate title
            last_title = stripped
        if 'director:' in stripped:
            if 'director:' in stripped and stripped.split('director:')[1].strip() == 'Peter Jackson':
                if last_title and last_title not in jackson_titles:
                    jackson_titles.append(last_title)

    line=raw.strip()
    if not line:
        continue
    if line.startswith('#'):
        continue
    if line.startswith('-'):
        # bullet
        if line.startswith('- director:'):
            director=line.split('director:',1)[1].strip()
            results.append((current_title,director))
        continue
    # otherwise title
    current_title=line
